record_type_quote: Utilizing Shah (2023)’s HRS cohorts (n = 8264, ages 66 to 101), and a sample from the Midlife in the United States (MIDUS) study (n = 5619, ages 40 to 75), we constructed the SFI-10 in both samples alongside an 8-item index (SFI-8) that reflects only social behavior.

targets.evidence_quote: Recently, Shah and colleagues (2023) developed a 10-item Social Frailty Index (SFI-10) in data from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) that used 8 social items plus age and sex to successfully predict mortality. This study evaluates the construct and criterion validity of the SFI-10.
targets.outcome_quote: Findings indicate that the SFI-10 relies heavily on age, with marginal contribution from its social items, to predict mortality in the HRS. Although social items had heightened importance for mortality prediction in MIDUS, the reliance on age persisted.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The mortality prediction persists in the independent MIDUS sample, although its interpretation as social frailty is challenged. Abstract evidence makes the exact correspondence uncertain.

reasoning: Identity matches title, authors and abstract citation ID. Conference abstract only, not a full article. New-sample MIDUS validation retests the SFI-10 mortality prediction; the same record also reanalyses original HRS cohorts. Classified as replication for its independent-sample component. No reference list supplies the original full author list, title or DOI. Construct-validity criticism is not itself failure of the original predictive finding.
